description: openCEM is an open-source capacity-expansion model for the Australian National Electricity Market. The project publishes a Python engine, setup instructions in its GitHub wiki and a separate repository of example inputs. A user supplies demand, generating-plant, technology cost and network assumptions; the engine selects investments and operations under the modelled constraints. Outputs are electricity-system capacity and dispatch results for the chosen planning horizon. Its published geography is the Australian National Electricity Market, and results depend on the study's spatial aggregation and time slices. The source is free under GPL-3.0. The repository calls itself a development version and advises at least 16 GB of RAM and an internet connection during runs. A limitation is that the public README leaves much model detail to a wiki whose last visible home-page edit was in 2019; users should check current input format and code version. openCEM supports power-supply planning. The catalogue's model-pypsa is a separate generic system modeller. No example inputs or solver was run.
inputs: Australian demand, fleet and technology cost assumptions
name: openCEM Australian capacity-expansion model
